name: Avanciq Accessibility Scanner
author: tradingcheckup

sections.description:
Avanciq Accessibility Scanner scans your published pages, posts and products for WCAG 2.2 level A and AA problems and tells you, in plain English, how to fix each one in WordPress.

It is a checker, not an overlay. It does not add any script to your public site and does not change what visitors see. Problems are fixed in your content and theme, where they really are.

What you get (all free, no account, no limits):

  • Scan the home page and up to 200 published pages/posts/products in one go, right from Tools > Avanciq Accessibility Scanner.
  • Each problem shows: what is wrong, how serious it is, which WCAG success criterion, how many places, an example element, and how to fix it in WordPress.
  • “Definite problems” and “check by hand” items are kept apart, so you are never told something passes when a person must look.
  • Dated evidence: download a CSV of every finding with the date and checker version, or print a report.
  • Draft accessibility statement built from your latest scan (never claims full compliance; edit before publishing).
  • A 10-point manual checklist for what automatic tools cannot see (keyboard, zoom, alt text quality, captions…).

Honest limits: automatic checks find only part of all accessibility problems. This plugin does not make a site “compliant” and does not protect you from legal claims. It is not legal advice.

Optional paid service – Proven Fix: if you add an Avanciq API key and tick consent, you can send one page at a time for a deeper scan. It confirms each problem with a second method and tests each suggested fix on a copy of the page in a real browser, then returns the fixed code. The plugin works fully without it.

External services

This plugin can connect to ONE external service, and only if you turn it on.

  • Service: Avanciq Accessibility API, hosted at api.tradingcheckup.com (same Australian business, ABN 66 763 463 348).
  • What it is for: the optional “Get Proven Fix” deeper scan.
  • When data is sent: only when an administrator has (1) saved an API key, (2) ticked the consent box in Settings, and (3) pressed “Get Proven Fix” on a page. Nothing is sent on activation, on page views, or in the background.
  • What is sent: the public URL of that one page and your API key. The service then loads the public page like a normal visitor. No visitor data, WordPress user data, passwords, cookies or private content are sent.
  • Terms of use: https://tradingcheckup.com/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://tradingcheckup.com/privacy

The free scan runs entirely in your own browser using axe-core (bundled, MPL-2.0) and sends nothing to anyone.

Privacy

Free scans run in the administrator’s browser. Results (page URL, rule ids, counts, short element snippets) are stored in one WordPress option on your own site (acchk_results) and removed when the plugin is deleted. Manual checklist ticks are stored in the browser (localStorage). The plugin sets no cookies, adds nothing to public pages and does not track anyone.

Credits

Uses axe-core 4.14.0 by Deque Systems, Mozilla Public License 2.0 (see assets/axe-LICENSE.txt). Source: https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core
sections.installation:
1. Install from Plugins > Add New, or upload the folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate.
  3. Go to Tools > Avanciq Accessibility Scanner, keep the pages ticked and press “Scan selected pages”.
sections.faq:
Does this make my site ADA / EAA compliant?

No tool can do that on its own. It finds many common problems and shows how to fix them. Manual checks and fixing the problems are still needed. This is not legal advice.

Why not an overlay widget?

Overlays add a script on top of your site; the underlying problems stay in the code. Many disability groups and courts have criticised that approach. We help you fix the source.

Some pages say “could not be scanned”.

A page that sends a strict security header (X-Frame-Options DENY or a Content-Security-Policy that blocks frames or scripts) cannot be loaded in the scanner frame. Allow same-origin framing (SAMEORIGIN) or scan that page with the optional Proven Fix service.

Is my data sent anywhere?

No, not for the free scan. See “External services” above for the optional paid service.
